assessment.answer: The score is high because the 8 inputs show a company whose liabilities are almost twice its assets (1.97 vs a peer median of 0.81), with a current ratio of 0.38, a $74.9 million net loss and $54.3 million of operating cash burn, all in the bottom 5-14% of peers. The filings confirm this is real distress, not an artefact: there is explicit going concern doubt, ongoing tax and SAFE-T note defaults, only $21.1 million of cash (about 4.7 months at the annual burn and less at the implied Q4 burn), and almost no non-cash relief in the loss. The late-2024 refinancing pushed most debt maturities to 2028 and the co-founder's entities keep funding the company, which offsets some of the risk, so I put it slightly above the band's base rate.
moved_by: Very short cash runway: $21.1 million of cash covers 4.66 months at the 2024 average burn, and the implied Q4 2024 operating burn (about $23.6 million, from $54.3 million for the year less $30.7 million for nine months) would use it up in about one quarter
Ongoing defaults on federal excise taxes ($7.7 million), California property taxes with a lien on four aircraft, and the SAFE-T note, plus missed PFG interest payments during 2024
Cross-collateralized financing agreements with minimum liquidity covenants, so one default could trigger acceleration and aircraft foreclosure
Almost all of the 2024 loss was cash (non-cash share about 3%), so the loss is not inflated by accounting charges

Offsetting (toward lower risk): the November 2024 refinancing pushed the LamVen $50.0 million note and the PFG $8.0 million note to December 31, 2028, and the $44.5 million Comvest term loan has a 4-year term with no required amortization
Offsetting: repeated funding from entities affiliated with the co-founder ($34.5 million related-party borrowings in 2024)

reasons.numbers: $818 thousand interest in arrears; default rate 15.75%; principal $8.0 million
reasons.quote: As of September 30, 2024, the Company was in arrears of $818 thousand in contractual interest payments due under the Convertible Note Purchase Agreement.

reasons.numbers: $122.6 million debt principal at December 31, 2024 vs $52.1 million at December 31, 2023
reasons.quote: As of December 31, 2024, we had $122.6 million in debt outstanding, representing principal related to term loans, related party promissory notes and convertible notes.
reasons.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, Item 1A Risk Factors - Previous defaults on debt

reasons.reason: Cross-default and minimum liquidity covenants mean a single breach could cascade, and the company already needed a PFG waiver of its $10 million minimum cash covenant during 2024
reasons.numbers: $10 million minimum cash covenant waived through December 31, 2024
reasons.quote: certain of our financing agreements are cross-collateralized, such that an event of default or acceleration of indebtedness under one agreement could result in an event of default under other financing agreements.

reasons.reason: Equity facility access is uncertain and capped, so it is not a reliable backstop for the short runway
reasons.numbers: $400 million total GEM commitment; only $2.5 million of GEM advances received in 2024; draws capped at 400% of 30-day average daily volume
reasons.quote: There can be no guarantee that we will be able to access any or all of the GEM Advances or other draw downs available under the Share Subscription Facility.
reasons.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, Item 1A Risk Factors - Share Subscription Facility

reasons.reason: NYSE listing deficiency on market cap and equity still being cured; the GEM facility depends on staying listed
reasons.numbers: Market cap and equity below $50 million; plan accepted August 21, 2024; 18-month cure period
reasons.quote: The NYSE accepted our plan on August 21, 2024. As a result, our common stock will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE during the 18-month cure period

reasons.reason: Growing fixed commitments for leased and ordered aircraft
reasons.numbers: 40 aircraft under operating leases (27 a year earlier); 90 Cessna Caravans committed
reasons.quote: As of December 31, 2024, we had 40 aircraft under operating leases, with an average remaining lease term of approximately 4.29 years.
reasons.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, Item 1A Risk Factors - Contractual obligations; Capital needs

reasons.reason: Management itself warns of restructuring or ceasing operations without new financing
reasons.quote: We may be required to cease operations which could result in our stockholders losing all or most of their investment.

evidence_against.point: The November 2024 refinancing moved the related-party LamVen debt into a $50.0 million secured convertible note due December 31, 2028, removing the string of short maturity extensions
evidence_against.quote: the Company issued a secured convertible promissory note (the “LamVen Note”) in aggregate principal amount of $50.0 million to LamVen, to refinance certain existing notes.

evidence_against.point: The PFG note maturity was pushed from December 31, 2024 to December 31, 2028, so the near-term maturity that cash could not cover is gone
evidence_against.quote: The maturity of the PFG Note is December 31, 2028, which may be accelerated upon the occurrence of certain events of default.
evidence_against.source: 10-Q, 2024-11-14, Note 19, Subsequent Events, Amendment to PFG Convertible Note Purchase Agreement

evidence_against.point: New 4-year Comvest term loan of $44.5 million (plus $5.5 million delayed draw) with no required amortization, backstopped by an HSBC letter of credit; this lifted cash from about $1.1 million in September to $21.1 million at year end
evidence_against.quote: pursuant to which the Company borrowed $44.5 million of term loans, and $5.5 million of delayed draw commitments.

evidence_against.point: Entities affiliated with a co-founder have repeatedly funded the company, providing $34.5 million of related-party borrowings in 2024
evidence_against.quote: A significant amount of funding to date has been provided by entities affiliated with a co-founder of the Company.
evidence_against.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, Item 1A Risk Factors - Financial Position and Capital Requirements

evidence_against.point: Financing inflows of $77.2 million in 2024 more than covered the $54.3 million operating burn
evidence_against.quote: net cash provided by financing activities was $77.2 million due to proceeds from borrowings under long term debt agreements, net of repayments, of $36.2 million, borrowings from related parties of $34.5 million
evidence_against.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, MD&A - Cash Flow from Financing Activities

evidence_against.point: Revenue nearly doubled and the net loss fell by about 70%, and current liabilities fell from $140.1 million to $89.6 million
The IRS offer-in-compromise pauses collection actions on the excise tax default while the company pays $34 thousand a month, so the tax default is not an immediate trigger
evidence_against.quote: In June 2024, the Company submitted a formal offer-in-compromise (“OIC”) to the IRS, seeking to resolve all excise tax liabilities.

evidence_against.point: The company regained compliance with the NYSE $1.00 minimum price standard
evidence_against.quote: The Company regained compliance with the requirements of Section 802.01C as of September 30, 2024.

evidence_against.point: The NYSE notice did not trigger a default under the company's debt agreements
evidence_against.quote: it does not conflict with or cause an event of default under any of the Company’s material debt or other agreements.

evidence_against.point: Asset sales brought in cash and cut net investing outflows to $3.6 million
evidence_against.quote: driven by an increase of $10.5 million in cash from sales of fixed assets
evidence_against.source: 10-K, 2025-03-21, MD&A - Cash Flow from Investing Activities
